results.content: # Machu Picchu Travel Restrictions 2025: Your Ultimate Guide. ## Machu Picchu Travel Restrictions: Ultimate Guide 2025. Planning a visit to Machu Picchu means knowing about *Machu Picchu entry permits* and *ticket reservation system*. **Restricted zones** like Huayna Picchu and Machu Picchu Mountain need separate permits. Book *Machu Picchu morning tickets* 2–3 months in advance for sunrise or mountain hikes. * **Machu Picchu Classic Ticket:** Grants 2.5 hours to explore Circuit 1 or 2, with entry at 6:30 AM or 12:00 PM. * **Machu Picchu + Huayna Picchu:** Allows 5 hours, including access to the iconic mountain via an 8:00 AM or 11:00 AM entry. All visitors to Machu Picchu must have *required tour guides* with them. Admin. § 115-17-12 - Commercial harvest of fish; legal species, seasons, size restrictions, daily limits, and possession limits. (a) The legal species of fish that may be taken under a commercial fishing permit shall be the following:. (3) common carp and exotic carp;. (b) None of the following shall be possessed by a permittee while in possession of commercial fishing gear or while transporting fish taken using commercial fishing gear:. (1) All species of fish excluded from subsection (a); and. (2) any species of fish listed in K.A.R. 115-15-1 or K.A.R. 115-15-2. The species of fish specified in this subsection shall be immediately returned unharmed to the water from which removed. (c) There shall be no size restriction on fish taken by a permittee. (d) There shall be no maximum daily or possession limit on the number of fish taken by a permittee. (e) No live specimen of bighead carp, silver carp, or black carp may be transported after commercial harvest. This regulation shall be effective on and after January 1, 2012. ## Notes. results.title: Anglers Face New Limits State Adds Restrictions in Length, Numbers
results.content: # Anglers Face New Limits State Adds Restrictions in Length, Numbers. Oklahoma anglers will discover some important changes in both creel limits and length limits at several state lakes this spring. Kim Erickson, Wildlife Department fisheries chief, said Altus-Lugert, Canton, Foss, Fort Cobb, Grand, Oologah and Tom Steed have been added to the list of lakes having an aggregate limit of 20 on those two species. Lakes already under the regulation include Great Salt Plains, Konawa, Fort Supply and Waurika. "This regulation is designed to protect hybrids which potentially could be harvested in great numbers without a creel limit," Erickson said. New length limits on black bass are also in effect on several more reservoirs. Erickson said a 14-inch minimum on largemouth, smallmouth and spotted bass has been imposed on lakes Carl Albert, Fort Gibson, Grand, Hudson and Thunderbird. The limit also applies to waters within these wildlife management areas: Atoka, Beaver River, Bolen Hollow, Gruber-Cherokee, Cookson, Ellis County, James M. Under this regulation, all black bass less than 14 inches in length must be released. "In general, these lakes either have histories of low reproduction and recruitment or are too small to allow unrestricted harvest of largemouth bass," Erickson said. Chimney Rock was added to the list of lakes with a 13- to 16-inch slot limit. All black bass between 13 and 16 inches long must be released. "Chimney Rock has a very dense population of bass under 13 inches," Erickson said. "We are stocking them annually with catchable-size catfish, but with a limit of 15, it doesn't take long to catch most of them out," he said. Finally, Erickson said Fort Supply Reservoir has become the first state lake to have a crappie length limit. All crappie less than 10 inches in length must be released. "Research has determined crappie fishing there can be improved by eliminating some of the peaks and valleys in the population, meaning those good years and bad years that occur regularly at Fort Supply," Erickson said. The limit on crappie at Fort Supply will be 15 per day. At other lakes, the daily limit on that species is 37.
